name: South Face / Standard Route
approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (Mountaineer Creek Trail #1599, elev. ~3,400 ft; Northwest Forest Pass required) at the end of Icicle Creek/Eightmile Road (FR 7601), follow the trail steadily uphill through forest along Mountaineer Creek. At about 2.5 miles, bear left at the signed junction onto the Colchuck Lake Trail (the right fork continues to Lake Stuart). Continue climbing, crossing a boulder-strewn section near the outlet, to reach Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft) at roughly mile 4, having gained about 2,000-2,100 ft — this is the last reliable water source before Aasgard Pass. Pick up the rough climbers' path along the lake's east/south shore (boulder-hopping in places) to its south end, then begin the well-known Aasgard Pass climb: an unrelenting, loose boot-track/goat-trail ascent of roughly 2,200 ft in under a mile to the 7,750-7,800 ft pass. This is the crux of the approach — footing is loose scree and talus lower down, the gully sections can be wet or icy, and snow commonly lingers into July, making an ice axe (and sometimes crampons/self-arrest practice) advisable; it is also a well-documented spot for slips given the sustained steepness and long runout. From the pass, work south to southwest across talus (and often a residual snow patch) toward the base of Dragontail Peak's east side, passing the west shore of Brynhild Lake and swinging around behind Witches Tower's distinctive summit spire to its south base — the pinnacle that divides the upper Snow Creek Glacier basin between Little Annapurna and Dragontail. All told, trailhead to the base of the tower is on the order of 6.5-7 miles one-way with roughly 4,700-4,900 ft of gain (consistent with the ~14-mile, ~5,400 ft round-trip car-to-car days reported by parties who do this as a single push). There is significant exposure on the ledge traverse near the top, and the Enchantments are prone to fast-building afternoon thunderstorms in summer, so an early start is standard practice.

approach_variants.name: Aasgard Pass, then past Brynhild Lake and around to the south side of the tower
approach_variants.notes:
From the Stuart Lake trailhead at about 3,400 ft, follow the Stuart Lake Trail south along Mountaineer Creek; at about 2.5 miles bear left at the signed junction onto the Colchuck Lake Trail. Cross Mountaineer Creek on logs and boulders — an awkward wet ford in early-season high water — and climb through forest and a boulder field to Colchuck Lake at 5,570 ft, roughly four miles in. Last reliable water.

Take the climbers' path along the lake's east and south shore through talus to the foot of Aasgard Pass, then up the eroded boot track: roughly 2,200 ft in well under a mile of loose scree and blocks, holding snow and ice into July.

From the pass at about 7,800 ft, work south to southwest across talus — initially as though heading for the snow route on Dragontail's east side — toward the tower, then up beside the west shore of Brynhild Lake (snow early in the season) and around behind the tower to its south base.

Figure six and a half to seven miles one way with something like 4,700-4,900 ft of gain.
approach_variants.season: Roughly Jul-Sep; earlier the traverse from the pass is a snow crossing and the slopes below the tower want an axe
hazards: Aasgard Pass: 2,200 ft of loose eroded scree with rockfall from parties above, holding snow into July
Serious exposure on the ledge traverse onto the east side of the tower
A four-foot slot that must be jumped to reach the true summit, with real consequence
Fast-building afternoon thunderstorms with no shelter in the Upper Enchantments
The downclimb off the south face is the crux for most parties
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The tower itself is the landmark — a distinct rock pinnacle standing alone at the west end of the Enchantments, dividing the upper basin between Little Annapurna and Dragontail. It is a pinnacle, not a summit on a ridge, so once you are close enough to see anything at all it is unambiguous.

Which side of it you want: the south side. From Aasgard Pass go up beside the west shore of Brynhild Lake (on snow early in the season) and swing around behind the tower to its south base. The scramble starts there: head up toward the band of white rock, pick up the ledge that leads around onto the east side, then climb the large black blocks to the top.

The discriminator: this line does not go to the col southwest of the tower, and it never needs a rope. If the ground ahead of you calls for one, you have left the scramble for one of the tower's roped lines.

Arrival confirmed by the summit itself: the top of this tower is guarded by a four-foot slot you have to jump. If you have scrambled to a high point and there was no slot, you are on a subsidiary block and not on the tower.

Grade check: nothing on this line is harder than Class 3. The ledge is easy but airy; take it slowly when it is wet or holds snow.
